subject: Invoice batching mismatch — EU VAT split on AR bucket
messages:
From: Oliver Kemp <okemp@stratusdata.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: VAT split on March batch - credits applied to wrong invoice

Hi Kimberly,

Quick note from our AP team: when we posted the March payment (batch 20270331-STR), two credit memos (SD-1234, SD-1240) were netted against an older net-amount invoice (INV-2026-091) instead of the open invoice INV-2027-004 that carries the EU VAT flag. That caused our VAT reclaim to be off by €14,320 on our end and looks like it triggered an unapplied balance in your AR for the same customer account.

Can you confirm whether Redwood ran an automated invoice batching rule for March that could have matched credits to the oldest open invoice? Our team can re-run allocations but we want to ensure you won't auto-close the older invoice first.

I've attached our payment allocation file and the credit memo PDF for reference.

Thanks,
Oliver
Accounts Payable
StratusData Ltd.

Attachments: payment_allocation_sheet.xlsx (xlsx) | credit_memo_SD-1234.pdf (pdf)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Kemp <okemp@stratusdata.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: VAT split on March batch - credits applied to wrong invoice

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the files. Short answer: our batching engine has a legacy fallback that prefers earlier outstanding invoices when invoice-level allocation metadata is missing. That would explain credits applying to INV-2026-091.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus, can you validate whether the credits were auto-applied by the March payout job (run id payout-20270331-2)?
- Lauren, can you confirm if we should do a manual journal correction (JE-2027-442) to move the credit from INV-2026-091 to INV-2027-004, or instead re-run allocation with explicit invoice IDs from Stratus?

Oliver — if you can confirm you want the allocation re-run (and are comfortable with us posting a reversing entry), we can proceed this week and send updated remittance advices.

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:22:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: VAT split on March batch - credits applied to wrong invoice

On Mon, 5 Apr 2027 at 10:05, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Kimberly —
>
> Thanks for the heads-up...

I pulled the payout logs and confirm payout-20270331-2 applied two credit memos to INV-2026-091. The allocation file attached to the payout message had empty allocation_invoice_id fields for both credits, so the engine defaulted to "oldest open" per the legacy rule.

Accounting preference: make a journal correction to reclass the credit application from INV-2026-091 to INV-2027-004 so audit trail remains clear. I'll prepare a JE CSV and route to Lauren for approval. Proposed entry: JE-2027-442 (reverse allocation on INV-2026-091, reapply to INV-2027-004; VAT lines adjusted to reflect EU VAT rate).

I'll attach the JE CSV to the follow-up once ready.

Marcus Lin
Manager, Revenue Operations

Please include the following in JE-2027-442: original_user_id, payout_run_id, source_file_name, and a short memo referencing StratusData remittance id 20270331-STR. Once I review and sign off I will schedule the JE for the April 6 morning posting window. Also confirm there are no FX impacts (Stratus paid in EUR, invoices in EUR).

I approve the journal correction approach rather than re-running allocations in the ledger because we want a single clear audit line for the movement.
